Class ClientHandlerRmi

java.lang.Object
it.polimi.ingsw.network.server.ClientHandler
it.polimi.ingsw.network.server.rmi.ClientHandlerRmi
All Implemented Interfaces:
ModelObserver
public class ClientHandlerRmi extends ClientHandler
Server-side RMI handler for a connected client.

Wraps the client's VirtualViewRmi stub and serializes all outgoing callbacks through the inherited messageSender executor, preventing concurrent RMI invocations on the same stub.

A background health check thread periodically pings the client via VirtualViewRmi.ping(). After MAX_FAILURES consecutive failures, the handler marks the client as disconnected and notifies the DisconnectionListener.

Design

Delegates to ClientHandler.sendAsync(CheckedRunnable) for each outgoing callback, reducing every onXxx() method to a single line. Idempotent disconnection and base health check logic are in the base class; this class adds only RMI-specific behavior (timeout-guarded ping, remote exceptions).

    • pingExecutor

      private final ExecutorService pingExecutor
      Dedicated single-thread executor that runs ping tasks in isolation, preventing a slow or hung RMI call from blocking the health check thread.

      A single thread is enough because only one ping is in flight at a time; using an unbounded cached pool would allow zombie threads to accumulate when RMI blocks indefinitely on a dead client (RMI is not interruptible via Future.cancel(boolean)).

  • Method Details

    • startHealthCheck

      protected void startHealthCheck()
      Starts the transport-specific health check thread.

      Called by subclass constructors after initializing network resources (e.g., RMI stubs, socket streams).

      Starts a daemon thread that pings the client every ClientHandler.PING_INTERVAL ms. Each ping is submitted to pingExecutor with a PING_TIMEOUT. TimeoutException or ExecutionException increments the failure counter; reaching MAX_FAILURES triggers disconnection.

      Specified by:
      startHealthCheck in class ClientHandler

    • handleTransportError

      protected void handleTransportError(Exception e)
      Handles a transport error during asynchronous send.

      Typically marks the client as disconnected and notifies the appropriate listener (e.g., DisconnectionListener, MatchManager).

      Handles a RemoteException that occurred during async sending: calls tryMarkDisconnected() and notifies the disconnection listener. Idempotent.

      Specified by:
      handleTransportError in class ClientHandler
      Parameters:
      e - the exception (RemoteException for RMI, IOException for socket)

    • tryMarkDisconnected

      protected boolean tryMarkDisconnected()
      Marks the handler as disconnected in an idempotent manner and shuts down the ClientHandler.messageSender.

      Subclasses owning additional executors or resources must override this method, call super.tryMarkDisconnected() first, and proceed only if it returns true: 

      @Override
protected synchronized boolean tryMarkDisconnected() {
    if (!super.tryMarkDisconnected()) return false;
    myExecutor.shutdownNow();
    return true;
}

      In addition to the base cleanup, shuts down the pingExecutor.

      Overrides:
      tryMarkDisconnected in class ClientHandler
      Returns:
      true if this thread was first to mark disconnection; false if already disconnected

    • injectGameVisitor

      public void injectGameVisitor(GameMessageVisitor gameVisitor)
      Injects a GameMessageVisitor into this observer.

      The default implementation is a no-op; observers that need to handle game-specific messages should override this method.

      Guards against null visitor: the visitor is set externally via ClientHandler.setVisitor(ClientMessageVisitor) after construction, so a race between visitor injection and game start could otherwise cause a NullPointerException.

      Parameters:
      gameVisitor - the visitor to inject

    • resetGameVisitor

      public void resetGameVisitor()
      Resets the injected GameMessageVisitor, removing any game-specific message handling from this observer.

      The default implementation is a no-op.

      Guards against null visitor for the same reason as injectGameVisitor(GameMessageVisitor).
